\projectText{The first revision used a fixed-gain proportional controller, which oscillated badly on tight corners. Moving to a full PID loop with gain scheduling based on error magnitude let the robot hold near-top speed on straights while slowing smoothly into turns.}

\projectPhoto{media/projects/line-follower-robot/pid-tuning.jpg}{Tuning session}{Logging sensor error against wheel speed to hand-tune PID gains.}

\projectText{Final lap times improved by 38\% over the proportional-only version, with zero track departures across 20 consecutive test laps.}

\projectOpen{3-DOF Desktop Robotic Arm}{Inverse-kinematics-driven pick-and-place arm}{Sep 2025 – Dec 2025}{Robotics, CAD, Kinematics}{SolidWorks, Arduino, Python}

\projectSummary{A three-degree-of-freedom robotic arm with a custom inverse kinematics solver, designed and 3D-printed from scratch for a desktop pick-and-place demo.
}

\projectPhoto{media/projects/robotic-arm/cover.jpg}{Assembled arm}{Full assembly with gripper attachment at rest position.}

\projectPhoto{media/projects/robotic-arm/cad-overview.png}{CAD overview}{Full linkage assembly modeled before any printing began.}

\projectText{Rather than use a lookup table, I derived closed-form inverse kinematics for the 3-link planar arm so any target (x, y) within the workspace maps directly to joint angles — no iterative solving needed on the microcontroller.}

\projectInteractiveFallback{media/projects/robotic-arm/gripper-jaw-render.png}{Gripper jaw (interactive)}{Drag to rotate — this is the actual print file for the final jaw geometry.}{3D MODEL}

\projectText{The gripper jaw went through four print iterations to get enough compliance to grip irregular objects without a force sensor, using a living-hinge geometry at the jaw base.}

\projectInteractiveFallback{media/projects/robotic-arm/pick-and-place-poster.jpg}{Pick-and-place demo}{Arm sorting objects by color using a webcam and OpenCV.}{VIDEO}


\projectClose

\projectSummary{A Synthetic Dataset Generator able to create thousands of unique, annotated training images of spesific parts from cad models. A smart dataloader able to train  Ultralytics YOLO CV models on randomized data sets based on a learning curve optimizing cirriculum. }
